what_it_does: Different programming frameworks for distributed computing systems (like Chapel, MPI, OpenSHMEM, Conveyors, and Lamellar) have dramatically different strengths and weaknesses when it comes to communication overhead and synchronization. This paper provides a comprehensive empirical comparison by implementing the same communication-intensive algorithm (distributed radix sort) across all five frameworks on large-scale HPE Cray supercomputers, measuring scalability, code complexity, and actual performance.
